market_mood: Risk-off continues: the S&P is down ~5% on the week while Anthropic's record $1.5T IPO soaks up capital and hawkish Fed minutes (officials expecting more hikes) press on gold, bonds and long-duration tech. Middle East supply risk is keeping a bid under oil even as the IEA flags weaker long-run demand.
self_check: My high-confidence calls have been badly wrong (14%) while low-confidence ones did best, and oil & energy is my worst theme, so today I kept confidence capped at medium, leaned on a bearish rates idea that has worked, and limited energy exposure to one small LNG idea.

picks.reason: Fed minutes show officials expecting more rate hikes, and a stronger dollar plus higher real rates have already pushed gold to a 14-month low; that pressure tends to persist for weeks.
Houthi missiles hit Riyadh's tallest tower and Saudi cities went on alert, which tends to drive Gulf orders for air and missile defense systems that RTX supplies.
Years of funded backlog and a dividend record, with Middle East risk back in the headlines.
Bond proxies struggle when the Fed is debating more hikes.

watchlist_notes.note: Oversold after a -4.8% week, with hawkish Fed minutes and the Anthropic IPO rotation driving the chop.
Tech is the worst sector of the week (-6.8%); the Anthropic listing is pulling money out of incumbent AI names.
Holding up slightly better than Nasdaq as money rotates toward value and staples.
No major company news; a Citi warning on tech outage risk is a sector-wide, not Apple-specific, story.
In the headlines mainly via Ackman's position and the AI capex debate the Anthropic IPO reignites.
Post-earnings digestion plus leadership uncertainty under interim CEO Kress; Anthropic's debut is the new AI benchmark investors are trading.
Its 14.6% Anthropic stake is now worth ~$161B, but Anthropic leasing its own data centers trims the long-run AWS story.
Also an Anthropic backer, but Anthropic reducing reliance on Google Cloud is a modest negative for future capacity bookings.
No major news beyond hedge-fund buying and the argument that its legal settlement masked a strong ad quarter.
Musk wants more exports from Shanghai as China sales fall, which points to soft domestic demand there.
Hawkish Fed minutes help net interest margins, though a Fed official's warning about AI bots moving deposits is a new operational worry.
Oil firmed on Houthi attacks and the tighter Iran blockade, but the IEA sees energy-security moves cutting demand 4% by 2035.
Still bruised: a 14-month low, a stronger dollar and Fed talk of more hikes keep the pressure on.
Minutes showing officials expecting more rate hikes are a direct headwind for long-duration Treasuries.

top_buys.pitch: A Fed that is talking about more hikes is the wrong backdrop for a non-yielding metal.
top_buys.why: October minutes show officials expecting further rate hikes and worrying about AI-driven inflation, which lifts real yields and the dollar. Gold has already fallen sharply from its January record and bounced only weakly off a 14-month low. The investment case erodes gradually, so this is a trend that can keep working rather than a one-day headline.
top_buys.risks: A sudden Middle East escalation or a soft inflation print could spark a quick safe-haven bounce in gold.
top_buys.watch: The next CPI release and Fed speakers' tone on a December move.

top_buys.pitch: Missiles landing on Riyadh's tallest tower tend to be followed by air-defense orders.
top_buys.why: Houthi strikes hit the Saudi wealth fund's headquarters and triggered alerts across southern Saudi cities, while the US tightens its blockade on Iran and Trump hints at more conflict after January 1. Gulf states restock interceptors and air-defense systems after episodes like this, and RTX is a primary supplier. Defense has lagged the market, so expectations are not stretched.
top_buys.risks: A genuine de-escalation after the Trump-Xi-Putin peace declaration would deflate the defense bid, and my recent geopolitics calls have been poor.
top_buys.watch: Any announced Gulf foreign military sales or supplemental US defense funding.

top_buys.pitch: Years of funded backlog and a dividend record, with Middle East risk back in the headlines.
top_buys.why: Coverage highlights defense primes sitting on billions in backlogged government orders, and renewed Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia plus a tightening Iran blockade support defense budgets. Northrop's revenue is largely contracted, which is defensive in a market down nearly 5% in a week.
top_buys.risks: Program cost overruns and a genuine Gulf de-escalation are the two obvious ways this fails.
top_buys.watch: Any new US or allied munitions and missile-defense contract awards.

top_buys.pitch: Bond proxies struggle when the Fed is debating more hikes.
top_buys.why: The October minutes show policymakers expecting further tightening, which lifts yields and makes high-dividend utilities less attractive. Utilities have held up better than most sectors this month, so there is more room to give back if rates keep rising.
top_buys.risks: The AI data-center power demand story is a genuine offset and could keep money flowing into utilities regardless of rates.
top_buys.watch: The 10-year Treasury yield and December Fed expectations.
